question: A school stationery cupboard held 223 folders at the start of term, and 110 of them went out to the new intake. 24 folders came back unused the following week. Each folder in the cupboard was filled with 4 workbooks, and every workbook contains 7 exercises. A dozen spare pens sit on the shelf beside them. How many exercises are there in the workbooks?

On Thursday morning a fishmonger took delivery of 29 boxes of sardines, with 5 trays packed in every box. During the afternoon he counted 8 fish on each tray. In the evening a late delivery added 16 more fish to the counter, and by closing time 1043 fish had been sold. A dozen cats waited by the back door. The price board is written in cents rather than in dollars. How many fish are left on the counter?

On Monday morning a physiotherapy clinic had 146 minutes of appointments in the diary, and the receptionist added 10 more before opening and another 25 at nine o'clock. The insurer pays 5 cents for every booked minute. In the afternoon it allowed a further 51 cents for equipment, and the second therapist, Noor, who sees fewer patients than her colleague Ilya, added 70 cents of materials to the claim. In the evening a late case added 8 cents. The claim form is filled in in cents rather than in dollars. How many cents does the claim come to?

A community hall had 177 notice boards in storage, and 45 of them were carried over to the annexe. The caretaker unscrewed all 6 screws from every board still in the hall. He sorted the loose screws into bags of 6, filling every bag completely. Each full bag was then closed with 4 staples. A dozen mops stood in the store cupboard. How many staples did the caretaker use?

A model shop had 120 kits on the shelf and a supplier sent 37 more before the holidays. Every kit contains 7 painted figures. Customers bought 984 figures over the season. A cancelled order then put 53 figures back on the shelf. How many figures are on the shelf now?

A bulb merchant planted 96 trays with 8 bulbs in every tray. 23 of the bulbs rotted in the wet spring and were dug out. A supplier sent 44 replacement bulbs, and a customer returned 61 that were never planted. The spring sale then sold 604 bulbs. How many bulbs does the merchant still have?

Kwame pressed 108 sheets of stamps, with 8 stamps on every sheet, and his colleague Ada, who presses fewer sheets than Kwame does, added 71 loose stamps to the same batch. Every stamp in the batch was perforated with 8 tiny holes. Each hole was then checked 2 times over by the inspection machine. The inspector recorded 1717 of those checks as failures. How many checks passed?

Lena's mill runs 137 looms, and each loom holds 6 reels of thread. Every reel is wound from 5 spools. A supplier sent 77 spare spools to the mill, and 22 spools arrived damaged and were thrown away. Each spool carries 8 lengths of thread, and every length is folded 6 times before packing. Lena's partner Georg runs fewer looms than she does at his own mill across the valley. How many folds are made in the mill's thread?

On Monday morning a bike courier set off with 135 envelopes and delivered 39 of them before ten o'clock. Before lunch a further 71 were dropped off on the second run. In the afternoon he found that every envelope still in his bag holds 7 documents. In the evening 34 of those documents were pulled out as duplicates, and each document that was left had to be stamped 4 times. How many stamps did the courier make?

A tram driver logged 19 trips last week, and each trip included 5 minutes of idling at the terminus. A new signal cut 26 of those minutes from the week, a rescheduled stop saved 46 more, and a quicker turnaround saved a further 4. The depot is charged 9 cents for every minute a tram spends idling. The bill is written in cents rather than in dollars. How many cents was the depot charged?

A school's lost property box held 88 items on Monday, and 49 of them were claimed by pupils during the week. The office added 31 items found in the yard, and the sports hall sent over 76 more. A charity collection then took 91 items away. Every item still in the box was photographed 9 times for the online list. A dozen parents came in to look through the box. The office logs the time spent on the list in minutes rather than in hours. How many photographs were taken?

On Monday morning a factory received 156 crates and divided them equally among its 4 assembly bays. Later that morning each crate in the first bay was opened and found to hold 5 machine parts. During the afternoon every part in that bay was fitted with 6 washers. In the evening a spare tin added 77 washers to the bay's stock. Each washer is dipped in 9 grams of grease before it goes on the line. How many grams of grease does the first bay need?

On Saturday morning a stationer had 90 boxes of pencils and split them equally between its 2 shops. In the afternoon the high street shop opened its boxes and found 4 packs inside every one. In the early evening the assistant counted 4 pencils in each pack. A late delivery added 26 loose pencils to the drawer, and 47 pencils were sold before closing. The shop's price list is written in cents rather than in dollars. How many pencils does the high street shop have?

A cake stall started the day with 59 sponge cakes, and 16 of them were bought whole by a caterer. Every cake still on the stall was cut into 3 slices. 35 slices went across to a coffee morning, 63 were sold at the counter, and 26 were taken to the staff room. A late bake then added 63 slices to the tray. The hall clock runs 15 minutes slow. The price card is written in cents rather than in dollars. How many slices are on the tray?

On Monday morning a transport company logged 189 minutes of driver training and added 32 minutes more before lunch. 26 minutes were cancelled when a trainer fell ill. In the afternoon a new safety course added 74 minutes to the schedule. The training centre charges 5 cents for every minute on the schedule, and in the evening head office decided to run the identical schedule at each of its 6 depots. A dozen drivers waited in the canteen for the news. The invoice is written in cents rather than in dollars. How many cents will the training cost?

A small airline had 227 seats on the evening flight, and 196 of them were booked online. 14 more were taken at the airport desk, and 1 was blocked off for a crew member travelling home. A cancellation later released 37 seats back into the pool. The booking screen shows flight times in minutes rather than in hours. How many seats are available on the flight?

A brickworks fired 72 racks in one week, with 4 trays on every rack and 3 bricks on every tray. A neighbour returned 25 bricks that had never been used on his extension. A garden wall job then took 529 bricks away from the yard. How many bricks are left at the works?

On Wednesday morning a phone shop had 157 handsets in the back room and 6 more arrived at lunchtime. During the afternoon the staff put every handset on charge for 9 minutes to test it. The supplier agreed to pay for 830 of those charging minutes. In the evening the shop was billed 6 cents for each of the minutes the supplier had not covered. The bill is written in cents rather than in dollars. How many cents was the shop billed?

A youth band has 15 members, and each member sold 6 tickets for the summer concert. The tickets were split equally among the 3 door staff for checking. One steward's pile was matched by a second batch exactly like it, so he held twice as many as before. His pile was then divided equally among the 3 entrance lanes. Each ticket in one lane is worth 6 raffle entries on the night. The hall has 400 seats. How many raffle entries do that lane's tickets give?

Yara had 67 minutes of studio time on her card and topped it up with 9 more. A long take used 47 minutes and a retake used another 3. Her bandmate Cai, who books far less studio time than Yara does, borrowed 17 minutes from her card. The studio refunded her 5 minutes after a power cut, then charged her 4 minutes for cleaning. The card is sold in minutes rather than in hours. How many minutes are left on Yara's card?

A charity cycle shop had 177 helmets on the racks and sold 65 of them at the summer sale. A donor returned 7 that had never been worn. The manager, Bea, sent 52 helmets to a partner project run by Otto, whose shop keeps fewer helmets than Bea's does. A school then donated 28 helmets to the shop. A dozen bicycles stood chained outside the door. The shop's price list is written in cents rather than in dollars. How many helmets does the shop have?

A swimming club had 110 kickboards in the pool store, and a school donated 17 more at the start of term. A supplier sent another 36 that same month. 109 kickboards were taken to the junior gala and never came back, and 4 split along the foam and were thrown away. A dozen lane ropes hang on the wall beside the store. How many kickboards are in the store?

A festival campsite has 226 pitches, and each pitch is staked out with 7 tent pegs. 517 pegs were lost in the mud over the weekend and never found. Every peg that did come back was cleaned with 7 strokes of a wire brush, and each stroke used 3 drops of oil. The campsite is 4 kilometres from the main stage. How many drops of oil were used?

On Monday morning Freya's team cut 239 sheets of glass, and every sheet gave 6 panes. Before lunch her colleague Piotr, who cuts fewer sheets than Freya does, added 26 panes from his own bench, then 14 more, and in the early afternoon another 19. Later that afternoon a glazing contract took 1460 panes away from the workshop. In the evening 17 panes cracked while they were being loaded onto the van. How many panes are left?

A school had 205 tablets in its charging trolley. 42 of them were sent away for repair and 128 were signed out by classes for the term. The tablets that were left were shared equally among the 5 after-school clubs. One club then had 4 of its tablets taken back by the office for an exam. The trolley itself cost 900 dollars. How many tablets does that club have?
